title: A more luminous distant star
hook: Change source luminosity and predict observed flux.
misconception: observed flux stays fixed when source luminosity doubles.
objective: Apply flux = L/(4πd²) to compare observed flux when source luminosity changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With an isotropic source at fixed distance in empty non-expanding space, flux = L/(4πd²). When source luminosity doubles, observed flux becomes 2 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model flux = L/(4πd²); scaling exponent 1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider an isotropic source at fixed distance in empty non-expanding space, with a nonzero initial result. If source luminosity triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on observed flux?
recall.why: Apply flux = L/(4πd²) under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 3.
